NEWS

Press Release:


Protea Glen Land Grabs
Protea Glen residents have warned illegal land invaders to stay away from a piece of land near the Soweto suburb, saying they will not tolerate the erection of shacks next to their homes. But the land invaders seem determined, resulting in violent clashes with police. According to research, the majority of land invaders are after residential spaces to be able to live closer to a working economy, rather than agricultural land. Has the invasion of land in Protea Glen turned the traditional notion of so-called land grabs on its head?


Script:


STRUCTURE – PROTEA GLEN

VO: With two thirds of South Africans living in cities, the demand for land has shifted from agricultural to urban.

Land in residential areas are now being targeted by illegal land grabbers, across South Africa - from Port Elizabeth to Ballito to Soweto in recent weeks.

GOOLAM: citizens in SA are frustrated – the ANC’s land approach has exacerbated apartheid style land displacement // INT1 M1

VO: Economist Goolam Ballim explains that today, the poorest individuals are often still the most remote from urban centres and industrial hubs, intensifying unemployment and inequality.

With the review of Section 25 of the Constitution to now provide for land expropriation without compensation – land reform has become increasingly contentious.

President Ramaphosa addressed the issue in parliament earlier this week.

UPSOUND: "If people think the issue of land will go away, wake up and smell the coffee, because the people of South Africa have made themselves clear.”

LINK: While accelerated land reform is a priority for the ANC, it appears to be moving too slowly for those on the ground, desperate for land. With communities taking matters into their own hands - any land, even in residential areas, appears to be up for grabs.

VO: In the first week of May, land invaders descended on the working class suburb of Protea Glen in Soweto, while the local councillor was able to diffuse the situation, the land grabbers returned a week later.

LINK: This week Protea Glen residents took a stand against land grabbers making brazen attempts to encroach on their township – they say the area has no space for shacks and illegal invaders //

PHELELANI: // once they occupy peace is gone – they are going to break in and steal from us. IN2 M9

VO: Phelelani Sindani represents the Protea Glen Crisis Committee – he says residents will not stand for invasions, and will protect the land and drive out land grabbers.

PHELELANI: we don’t say everyone that lives in a shack is a potential criminal // there is this myth that we who stay in bond house, that we are rich, everything is , we have insurance – they can breaking and steal our things – we want to avoid all those things. IN2 M2

VO: Terence Corrigan is from the Institute of Race Relations.
TERENCE: What we are seeing in Protea Glen – foothole into formal property ownership – having this new community springing up – concerns about crime, property values, no less in Sandton than in Soweto. INT1 M9

VO: Gauteng Human Settlements MEC Dikgang Uhuru Moiloa insists lawlessness will not be tolerated.

MEC: // we are sympathetic to people that are looking for houses, but land grab is a no-no for Gauteng and where such happens we will unleash the state security to restore law and order. This country has to work. INT1 M13

VO: But the people of Protea Glen feel authorities need to protect vacant land from invaders and took the streets to protest.

PHELELANI: // councillor relaying message to his authorities but it seems that they are ignoring him. IN1 M5 // – they’ve sent a junior to engage with us – a driver – not a decision maker – now it is an emergency, we need a decision maker. IN2 M6

VO: The protest resulted in a stand off with the police after the closure of the R559 in Protea Glen. Chaos erupted when police used rubber bullets, stun grenades and tear gas to disperse the community.

PHELELANI: They came in here – it is us who are assisting gov in protecting land // instead of shooting of come and protect the land,– but don’t shoot at us. IN2 M4

VO: But Captain Kay Makhubela points out there are procedures to deal with land invaders and residents can’t just protest and barricade roads – that, is also illegal.

CAPTAIN KAY: // their responsibility is to inform the police or to report to the relevant authority so that we can come make sure that those people occupying the land without authority are being removed immediately // IN1 M4

VO: But the issue of residential invasions will not be easily resolved according to Corrigan.

TERENCE: // One of the first and most primal needs is a place to stay – people will pretty much trample over anything to find that settlement // INT1 M6 // Urban land becomes a prized commodity //INT1 M7

GOOLAM: there are pockets of SA society that are hungry to farm – land hunger not land and seed hunger – people want to be urbanised, proximate to economic centres // INT2 M1

VO: Phelelani says they are not against progress and land reformation.

PHELELANI: All we are saying before anyone can occupy it needs to be services – there is no sanitation there, there is no electricity system there. What they are going to do when they occupy that land they are going to tap into our homes for electricity // IN2 M1

VO: Putting in infrastructure for services after an informal settlement has been established is extremely challenging says MEC Moiloa. He believes the Protea Glen property owner grievances are legitimate.

MEC: //They are saying we don’t want squatter camps next to our houses, and that is justified because negative equity is a consequence of putting something that doesn’t have value next to someone who is spending his sweat in an investment for his family to pay a bond for 20 years.. INT1 M13

LINK: The economic hubs of South Africa are seen as the gateway to prosperity – drawing people from far and wide seeking opportunities in the cities. While this feeds a growing demand for housing, effective land reformation policies have yet to become a reality.

VO: Authorities need to change their approach to empowering people to build their own economic futures says Corrigan.

TERENCE: As long as government assumes the role of benevolent protector and distributor of resources this is going to remain a hot button issue with no resolution. INT1 M14 //

VO: Land transformation could have moved faster, preventing the wider unease and angst it now represents in the current economic and political climate says Ballim.

GOOLAM: over last decade SA in economic malaise // and combined with this land hunger// it’s created cocktail of unease – in an environment of populism, a year away from elections it seems to be building to steamy head …INT2 M6

VO: While some political parties appear to be adding fuel to the fire.

JULIUS UPSOUND: when we say occupy land – we don’t say do it illegally – it is the right thing to do – it is your land.

VO: MEC Moiloa says calls like that are simply irresponsible.

MEC: I reject it with the contempt that it deserves, // You are basically saying people must move onto land they must not have sanitation, without water, without electricity - just what are you saying as a leader// INT1 M18

VO: But it goes beyond just service delivery, effective spatial development is crucial says Ballim.

GOOLAM: // South African society has not embraced the notion that SA needs to have an integrated society – a more recent concept – developers encouraged to include in their broader plans social housing along side more affluent housing – the idea of spatial planning a more latter day concept and somewhat belated. INT2 M3

VO: An issue the MEC is trying to address with the introduction of Human Settlement Mega Cities.

MEC: the modern way of planning for human settlement is that you must work in a place where you sleep – // INT1 M33 // these are not just HS for the sake of it – it is part of the modernisation, transformation and re-industrialisation of the GP province INT1 M30

VO: But these projects won’t be completed in the near future.

MEC: development is a subject of budget and available resources and unfortunately resources are always scarce in development economics – it is a question of looking carefully at the available resources and allocating them accordingly to the affordability of the municipality, of the country..INT1 M29

VO: With the drive towards urbanisation, the demand for land in residential areas is not going to resolve itself.

GOOLAM: this is a trend and a land hunger that must be satisfied and the ruling party is going to have to pay far more attention to. INT2 M1

VO: In the meantime, Captain Makhubela says the police are committed to upholding the rule of law.

CAPTAIN KAY: if they are coming in to occupy the land without permission they will meet us, they will find us on the ground – we are going to deal with them according to the law. IN1 M7

VO: But Phelelani says the community will remain on high alert.

PHELELANI: We don’t want a situation where these people come at night and invade – in the morning when we wake up there are more shacks – then there will be more confrontation and we don’t want that type of situation. IN1 M6

PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Landgrabbers are targeting residential areas across South Africa as the demand for land shifts from agricultural to urban. But the community of Protea Glen are making as stand against illegal invasions.

PROMO 2
VO: The residents of Protea Glen came under fire in their efforts to protect vacant residential plots from land grabbers in a standoff with police.

PHELELANI: instead of shooting of come and protect the land – but don’t shoot at us. IN2 M4

PROMO 3
VO: As the demand for land shifts from agricultural to urban – residential plots are being targeted by illegal land invaders – raising questions about property owner rights.

TERENCE: concerns about crime, property values, no less in Sandton than in Soweto


PROMO 4
VO: The debate around land expropriation without compensation is an increasingly contentious issue, as South Africans desperate for land, become impatient.

Goolam: a year away from elections it seems to be building to steamy head …INT2 M6

JULIUS UPSOUND: // we don’t say do it illegally – it is the right thing to do – it is your land.

VO: And now as, land grabbers set their sights on residential areas across the country authorities say this lawlessness will not be tolerated.

MEC: // And where such happens we will unleash the state security to restore law and order. INT1 M13
